title: The profiler crashes threads
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5 beta 1 mono through 4.5 beta 6 mono
- Not reproducible in: 4.2.2 stable, 4.3 stable, 4.3 stable mono, 4.4.1 stable mono, 

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta6.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - AMD Ryzen 9 7950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

I'm making a system for parallel processing of multiple tasks. My game crashes with a seemingly rare error when the profiler is active. It happens with loose Threads and also with WorkerThreadPool, but it does not crash if only using exactly one thread. 

```
E 0:00:10:146   repro-threads.gd:38 @ wait_us(): Internal bug, please report: CowData was modified during destruction.
  <C++ Error>   Condition "_ptr != nullptr" is true.
  <C++ Source>  ./core/templates/cowdata.h:270 @ _unref()
  <Stack Trace> repro-threads.gd:38 @ wait_us()
                repro-threads.gd:32 @ _task()
                repro-threads.gd:18 @ _worker_loop()
```

### Steps to reproduce

steps to reproduce:
- run attached simple project
- enable debugger if it's not set to autostart
- observe errors and crash.

- for science, put `repro-WorkerThreadPool.gd` onto the scene Node and see that it still happens.

or you can just throw this code onto a blank Node in a new project and run it with the profiler enabled:

```gdscript
extends Node
# the goal is to see how many 30us operations i can squeeze out of any amount of threads

const THREAD_COUNT := 10
var workers := []
var result_queue := []
var queue_mutex := Mutex.new()

func _ready():
	for i in THREAD_COUNT:
		var t := Thread.new()
		workers.append(t)
		t.start(_worker_loop.bind(i))

func _worker_loop(_i):
	var result:bool
	while true:
		result = _task(0)
		queue_mutex.lock()
		result_queue.append(result)
		queue_mutex.unlock()

 ## reports how many times the operation was run in the last [counter_max] frames
func _process(_delta):
	queue_mutex.lock()
	print(result_queue.size())
	result_queue.clear()
	queue_mutex.unlock()


func _task(_i: int) -> bool:
	wait_us(30)
	return true

func wait_us(us:int):
	var end_time:int = Time.get_ticks_usec() + us
	while Time.get_ticks_usec() < end_time:
		pass
```
